newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo to lay off civil servants.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo to lay off civil servants.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's Congo is to lay off "fictitious" civil servants in a drive to reform the public sector and improve the economy after decades of mismanagement under ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.

Finance Minister Mawapanga Mwana Nanga told a news conference on Saturday that lists drawn up earlier this week to facilitate salary payments to long-suffering civil servants had shown that the public sector had to be "cleansed".
"We have to get rid of fictitious workers and those with fake credentials. We need an efficient public administration. There are people who were placed there for political reasons," Mawapanga said.
He said the vast central African country's civil servant payroll was estimated at 470,000 and that about $10 million was due to be spent on their salaries this month.
"We want to eradicate unemployment. To this end we have to remove those who think they work, but don't. We don't want fictitious workers any more," he said.
Economists say the unemployment rate in the nation of over 40 million hovers at about 70 percent of the workforce. No official figures are available.
Many civil servants collected their meagre wages for the first time in six months last week.

They expected Kabila, who declared himself president of the former Zaire last month, to improve their working conditions, and most were disappointed to receive the same low salary, ranging from $9 to $38, as they did under Mobutu.
Public employees have to have other work to make a living, trading anything from cigarettes to home-grown vegetables.
Some are so demoralised that they only turn up in the crumbling public administration building in Kinshasa city centre three times a week.

"We will see in the future how we could allow rises. We admit that their salaries are low. But it's high time that the state stops spending much more than it earns. If we improve our revenue, then we will look into the question of salaries," Mawapanga said.

State television said on Saturday that tax receipts in Kinshasa alone rose to a record $6.5 million in June from $2.5 million in May. It said the money used to go into corrupt officials' pockets instead of the state coffers.

Mobutu, who fled into exile in Morocco, is said to have stashed away billions of dollars abroad. The official Moroccan news agency MAP said on Saturday that he had undergone an operation in the Moroccan capital, Rabat, after "serious bleeding complications".
